circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. As the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit after Bahrain, it preceded later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various supporting racing events. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 classification for its facilities and safety standards.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit hosted the Austrian Grand Prix during two separate eras: initially from 1970 to 1987 under its original name, and again from 1997 to 2003 following a redesign and shortening of the track. The venue underwent significant modifications between these periods before adopting its current identity.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, positioned along Baku Boulevard with a lap distance of 6. 003 km, ranking it as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and holds the distinction of hosting the Middle East's inaugural Formula One race. The venue, which maintains a FIA Grade 1 license, accommodates multiple racing series including Formula One's annual Grand Prix, GP2 Series, and various endurance events, with several configurable track layouts available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657-kilometre Spanish motorsport venue features a balanced combination of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for racing machinery. The FIA Grade 1 certified facility accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km circuit in Belgium that has hosted the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1950, when it was included in the inaugural F1 season. The track has maintained an annual presence on the championship calendar from 1985 onward, with only brief absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre track that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its role in international single-seater racing, the circuit has accommodated various other major motorsport series including sports car championships and North American open-wheel competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading hosts China's premier motorsport events, most notably the Chinese Grand Prix which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, situated in Northamptonshire, England, has served as the venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After rotating among three British circuits from 1955 to 1986, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, while the track also features on the MotoGP calendar.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it debuted in 1986. Built remarkably quickly in just eight months near a major highway after plans for a Monaco-style street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected, the inaugural race was dedicated to János Drapál, a pioneering Hungarian motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit built in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track has hosted the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949 (except during 1980 renovation), making it one of only four circuits on the Formula One calendar since the championship's start, and earns its "Temple of Speed" nickname through its notably fast straights and high-speed corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, and managed by Honda's Mobilityland subsidiary. The track hosts major international racing events, particularly Formula One and Japanese Super Formula championships, and accommodates up to 155,000 spectators.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its concentration of major hotels and casinos. The layout incorporates several of the region's iconic landmarks, creating a unique urban racing environment for Formula One competition.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City commemorates two fatal racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix twice previously on an alternate configuration before its most recent hosting period began in 2015, now marketed as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium in Florida, spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and achieving average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, the track joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 and has since hosted the Miami Grand Prix annually.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, incorporating the harbour area of the principality. It is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its primary location within the Monte Carlo neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until the partnership concluded in 2026. The venue, situated close to the North Sea, had previously operated under different names before adopting its current sponsorship designation in 2025.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari motor racing venue situated north of Doha near the city of Lusail. This FIA Grade 1 facility spans 5. 419 kilometers with a principal straightaway measuring 1.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The venue hosts major motorsport events and contains additional facilities including a karting track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront, serving as the venue for the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural Formula One race in 2021.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating portions of the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km Spanish motorsport venue features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing various driving skills. The track holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 facility situated in Austin, Texas, serving as the venue for Formula One's United States Grand Prix alongside major motorcycle and endurance racing events. The track has hosted numerous racing series including IndyCar and various sports car championships throughout its operational history.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver competing for Williams in Formula One under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two World Drivers' Championships in 2005 and 2006 with Renault, along with 32 Grand Prix victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the only driver to win both Formula One's and endurance racing's world titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed eight Grand Prix victories following his series entry in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British driver currently racing in Formula One with the Haas team. He has established himself as a competitor in motorsport's premier series.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto is a Brazilian motorsport competitor currently driving for Audi in Formula One.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas has established himself as a consistent midfield and podium competitor throughout his 13-season Formula One career, securing two runner-up finishes in consecutive championship campaigns while racing for Mercedes. Now competing for Cadillac, Bottas has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories across his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas while primarily competing in European endurance racing with Nielsen Racing's LMP2 programme. He made seven Formula One appearances across the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who represents France in Formula One, currently racing for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved a record-tying seven World Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's total. He holds numerous sport records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in Formula One history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing extensive experience from a successful career across multiple racing disciplines. His accomplishments include victory at the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans endurance race in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, races for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished second in the drivers' championship in 2022 and has achieved nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver who has competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he races for BMW in the World Endurance Championship with WRT as a factory driver, while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver racing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One drivers' title after competing for eight seasons in the sport. He has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon currently races in Formula One for Haas. He achieved his sole Grand Prix victory in 2021 at the Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac and brings extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri has secured nine Formula One race victories during his time competing for McLaren across four seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One over a 14-year span from 2011 through 2024, earning eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," he established himself as a consistent competitor throughout his time in the sport before retiring from racing.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British driver, has claimed eight Grand Prix victories while competing for Mercedes across his eight-year Formula One career.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, bringing experience from 12 seasons of competition. Throughout his career, he has achieved four Grand Prix victories.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who recently concluded his Formula One tenure spanning 2023 to 2024. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously raced in IMSA's LMP2 class for Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held a full-time Formula One position across five seasons starting in 2021 before transitioning to a reserve capacity in 2026 with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag and has secured four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles from 2021 to 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, he has accumulated 73 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One, having previously competed as a full-time driver between 2022 and 2024. He remains the sole Chinese national to have participated in the sport's premier racing series.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone outfit rebranded as Alpine from 2021 onwards, maintaining its identity as Renault's factory team while promoting the French manufacturer's Alpine sports car brand through sponsorship deals. After competing under the Renault banner for several years, the team operated under Alpine's name until Renault's withdrawal from the sport concluded at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin is a British manufacturer with a recurring presence in Formula One, currently competing under the AMR GP Limited entity as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, has participated in every Formula One World Championship since 1950, making it both the sport's longest-running and most accomplished team. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the outfit remains a cornerstone of the championship's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American-licensed Haas Formula competes in Formula One following its 2016 debut, founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014. The squad underwent a leadership transition when team principal Guenther Steiner departed in early 2024, with Ayao Komatsu assuming the role.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: The Swiss engineering firm Sauber, established by Peter Sauber in 1970, became a Formula One constructor from 1993 onwards while maintaining success in endurance racing, including a Le Mans victory in 1989. Following numerous iterations during its three-decade F1 tenure, the team departed the championship in 2025 as motorsport's fourth-longest-running independent constructor, subsequently being acquired by Audi AG to serve as the foundation for its factory F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited, a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Woking facility, operates as a subsidiary within the wider McLaren Group structure and is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with its current team based in Brackley and holding a German licence. The modern Mercedes-AMG Petronas operation became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Toto Wolff, and Ineos from January 2022, with each holding equal stakes. The marque is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" in racing circles.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as the second team within Red Bull's racing portfolio. Based in Faenza with a Milton Keynes facility adjacent to its sister squad, the team operates as a constructor alongside Red Bull Racing under Austrian ownership.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned operations alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad represents the Austrian conglomerate's second constructor entry on the grid.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has been a Formula One fixture since 2005 and represents one of two F1 squads owned by Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner led the team from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies assuming the leadership role thereafter.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerging from the remnants of Williams's prior racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and has established itself as a significant presence in the sport's history.
